outcome_summary: Died after prolonged retreats while starving; exact cause unconfirmed
improvements: When escaping toxic gas, the bot now avoids gas-free ground that it already recognizes as part of a hazardous special room, rather than treating every clear tile as a safe destination.
incoming_learnings: Gas-free ground is not necessarily a safe exit: preserve recognized piranha-bank and other special-room exclusions when choosing a gas escape. Reobserve after each step, retain unfinished loot honestly, and keep terminal exhaustion rather than restoring repeated waits. A corrected selection does not establish successful escape or puzzle completion.

review.review: The hero died after a loot-directed move at one HP; decision 1266's accepted transition confirms death but not an unambiguous killer. Starvation was public, and potion identities revealed afterward were not available beforehand. There were no planner incidents. Earlier, repeated doorway retreats failed to establish a flight-aware hold. The focused defect is decision 1116: the bot committed to door 299 even though its observed surroundings already failed every existing holding-square check against the two flies. Decisions 1116–1118 reached that door, and decision 1119 reported the predicted missing hold. The proposed narrow preflight rejects such fully observed, unusable flying-enemy setups while retaining unknown-perimeter reconnaissance and arrival checks. An isolated public-geometry fixture reproduces the original commitment; the candidate chooses the existing ordinary retreat without claiming a choke. The new regression fails as expected on original source and passes on the candidate; the full suite passes 2104 tests with four skipped. This does not establish successful escape or that this defect alone caused death.
review.learnings: Before committing to a doorway against flying pursuers, use already observed geometry to rule out doors with no viable holding square. Keep unknown-side reconnaissance distinct from verified refuge, preserve mandatory pickups and hazard gates, and do not equate a corrected plan with successful escape.
